author: TEDx Talks
description:
Art and music are extensions of who we are as human beings. 

Join Alex Van Halen + David Lee Roth, members of the legendary rock band Van Halen, and world renowned muralist Robert Vargas as they they examine how stepping outside of comfort zones, absorbing foreign cultures, and embracing contrasting creative approaches can enrich your work. Discover how keeping an audience within arm's reach allows creators to build genuine community through their craft. Alex Van Halen helped redefine the sound and spirit of rock & roll. Born in Amsterdam in 1953, he moved with his family to Pasadena, California, in 1962, where he and his younger brother, Eddie, began their lifelong creative partnership. Originally trained in classical piano and guitar, Alex found his voice behind the drums. In 1972, the brothers co-founded Van Halen, launching a band that would become one of rock's most influential acts. With his thunderous playing, signature double-bass technique, and massive custom drum kits, Alex
title: Why great art requires risk | Alex Van Halen, David Lee Roth & Robert Vargas | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Speaker and composer David Snyder, based in Los Angeles, CA, shares the deeply personal story of how nine years of rigorous classical piano training shaped — and nearly broke — his identity as an artist. 

Through live music and original composition, the talk explores how discipline and rules aren't the enemy of creativity, but the foundation of it. Drawing from his own journey of quitting the piano after a devastating competition loss, moving to LA, and eventually becoming a professional musician and composer, the talk makes the case that you have to learn the rules before you can truly break them. Woven throughout with live piano performance — including an original composition written for his wife — the talk ultimately reveals what so many artists discover: that music can say the things we don't have the words for, and that our greatest creative breakthroughs often come from the very experiences that first seemed to destroy us. 
To learn more about David Snyder and his work, visit t
title: How I Failed as a Musician - So I Could Become an Artist | David Snyder | TEDxFargo

author: TEDx Talks
description: Have you ever watched a science-fiction movie and wondered just how much of it could actually be possible? Have you ever seen a cool invention on screen and wondered if someone had managed to make something similar in reality? This talk aims to explore to what extent some of the core aspects of science-fiction movies could be re-created in real life, including AI and robots, aliens and space travel, and biologically enhanced and mutated beings. Sara Davis is a student in the Lower Sixth studying Mathematics, Chemistry and French. She hopes to study Chemistry or Linguistics at university, and is particularly interested in real world applications and possibilities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What if movie science could exist? | Sara Davis | TEDxFrancis Holland School Sloane Square

description:
As cities rise ever higher, why do people become increasingly disconnected from wind, trees, and the changing seasons? Landscape architect Wanpeng Zu begins with the concept of a "climbable mountain forest," bringing nature back into high-rise architecture. Through the exploration and everyday experiences of its users, the space gains an unexpected vitality. Sustainability is no longer just an idea on paper, but becomes part of daily life — transforming a space drawn by designers into a city truly lived by its people. 1、Global Urban Public Realm Explorer
2、Design Director at TLS | M.S. in Architecture and Urban Design, Columbia GSAPP

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In ecological restoration on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, high-tech solutions are not the only answer. Instead, Trachung Barang chose to return to the old ways—applying the time-honored, traditional knowledge passed down through generations of Tibetan herders to heal the land. Working with the rhythm of nature, he used the very hooves of livestock to trample seeds into the soil and their manure to nourish it, all while practicing scientific rotational grazing. This approach has successfully revived the once-desertifying grasslands, bringing them back to life.
His unwavering commitment embodies the true essence of sustainable development: respecting the land, revering nature, and trusting the pace of time. Like the resilient grass that anchors itself firmly in the earth, he guards the green of his homeland with a lifetime of patience. 1、20-Year Grassland Restoration Pioneer & Desertification Fighter
2、Recipients of “Rangeland Restoration Awards 2026”
3、The Subject of "Palzang the Herds
title: 20 Years of Healing: The Rebirth of My Hometown Grassland | Trachung Palzang | TEDxWukang Rd

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The ecological crisis we face is, at its core, a crisis of perception. Through artificial intelligence, emotion technology, and interdisciplinary artistic practice, Alex Long Yuan transforms the subtle respiration of plants, the passage of time inscribed in tree rings, and fluctuations in human emotion into powerful experiences of light, sound, and space.
Inner sustainability forms a foundation for rebuilding our relationship with the world. True sustainability is not about humanity positioning itself above nature and attempting to “save” the Earth, but about rediscovering our resonance with the living world and relearning how to belong to this planet. 1、International Interdisciplinary Contemporary Artist
2、Emotion Tech Innovator. Co-founder of INOASIS
3、Sole Commissioned Artist for the UN Forest for Life Project This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description: Music has become this fundamental aspect of our lives. We as society cannot function without it. This talk will revolve around how the 1960s has transformed the way society uses and views music. How it has turned from this simple entertainment, into a global cultural phenomenon. How because of the 60s music has shaped identity, politics, and emotions. From artists like Jimi Hendrix, creating an entirely new genre of music, using distortion and feedback. To the Beatles making tours an experience shared by the whole world. My talk will argue how all aspects of modern music, streaming, festivals, tours, genres, can be traced back to the 60s. Gabriella Calice is a student in the Lower Sixth studying English literature, Economics, and German. I hope to study economics at IE university. author: TEDx Talks
description:
A devastating super typhoon that destroyed city infrastructure unexpectedly revealed humanity's deep desire for connection and play during desperate times. Amidst widespread power outages, Becca Liu transformed a ruined playground into a kinetic power station, turning children's physical play into actual electricity to light up the community. True community resilience relies not just on the power grid, but on the warmth of human connection. Joy and hope are ultimately the most powerful forces that help us weather the storm and rebuild our homes. 1、Founder and CEO of HappyPower
2、IUCN Global Changemaker
3、China National Coordinator for the Asia-Pacific Sustainable Forum This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

author: TEDx Talks
description:
AI can already produce a flawless deck in five minutes. Qi Zhai-McCartney calls that amazing and suffocating in the same breath, and argues we cannot out-execute the machine on output, which means the question everyone is asking is the wrong one.

Qi is the founder of Atlas Therapy & Coaching, a finance professional turned psychotherapist and couples therapist who has lived in six countries and nine cities. She makes the case for Relational Intelligence as the essential skill of the AI era rather than a soft one.

Drawing on the 88-year Harvard Study of Adult Development, Amy Cuddy's work on first impressions, Harlow's monkeys and polyvagal theory, she offers three relational truths: warmth matters more than competence, stop solving and start witnessing, and co-regulate before you argue the facts. We are human beings, not human doings. Qi Zhai-McCartney is a psychotherapist, coach, & founder specializing in Relational Intelligence, the "human technology" required for today’s hyper-rat
title: Room to Be Human: Our Future is Relational | Qi Zhai- McCartney | TEDxAsia Pacific U

author: TEDx Talks
description:
At six years old, Sharanya Rao wanted nothing more than to skip her Sunday morning dance class and go play with her friends. Fifteen years later, she cannot imagine who she would be without it.
For many, a classical art form is something to be pursued up to a point:an Arangetram, an exam, or until a busy academic life gets in the way. But what if we have been looking at it all wrong? What if the value of an art form lies not in the career it might create, but in the person it quietly shapes along the way?
In this talk, she explores the many ways an art form can become a second education: teaching us how to balance seemingly different paths, step outside our familiar circles, build relationships with mentors, and develop an inner world that academic life alone may not provide.

title: How classical artforms equip you for life | Sharanya Rao | TEDxRVCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We usually consider digital security as something that exists completely in the world of software.

However, what happens when the underlying secrets behind such protection mechanisms are also in peril? In fact, keeping our digital world safe needs hardware mechanisms in place.
Isha Oswal talks about the importance of hardware encryption and about how physical protection systems can make the protection of sensitive data even stronger. In particular, she focuses on the need to work with the protection and storage of cryptographic keys and the concept of hardware security.

In this talk, we get a completely new view of digital security as the focus moves from software solutions and encryption tools to the physical element that can help with the protection of sensitive information. In particular, she elaborates on how hardware-based solutions can help in data safety, trust, and dealing with digital challenges. Isha Oswal is CEO of JISA Softech, one of India's leading cybersecurity compan
title: The hidden hardware protecting your digital life  | Isha Oswal | TEDxVIT Pune

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often consider travel as a checklist of destinations: the places that everyone tells us we must visit; the famous landmarks, the crowded streets. But what if travel is much deeper than that? What if the actual essence of travel is something we experience along the way? 

In this insightful talk, Chanak Doshi redefines the traditional way of looking at offbeat travel, shifting the focus beyond hidden destinations to actual meaningful experiences. He also explores how well-planned offbeat tourism can support the locals and help boost the economy of the country.
This talk gives one a new way to look at offbeat travel, beyond choosing lesser-known destinations and towards valuing experiences and local connections. It offers a perspective on travelling responsibly while discovering the deeper stories that make a journey truly memorable. Chanak Doshi is the founder of Simply Offbeat Holidays, a travel company focused on meaningful, community-led, and offbeat experiences across India and
title: Redefining Offbeat Travel | Chanak Doshi | TEDxVIT Pune

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her talk, Harini Iyer describes her journey from feeling out of place in her surroundings to channelling those exact differences into her personal strengths and creative work. Through heartfelt storytelling and her mesmerizing Carnatic interpretations of popular Jazz standards, she conveys that music can bridge the gap between different roots, languages and communities.

The displacement she felt in her roots helped shape who she is today, which led to her forming a community of musicians combining Indian classical music and Jazz and eventually creating the Tamil Jazz Collective. With her love for the stage and music, she encourages the audience to ask themselves who they want to become when the surroundings don't fit, and if they’re willing to push the boundaries and explore uncharted realms. Renowned for her captivating fusion of classical Indian music with contemporary genres such as Soul, Pop and Jazz. Iyer is the founder and the creative director of the Tamil Jazz Collective.
title: Building when you don't belong | Harini Iyer | TEDxRVCE

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your morning cup of coffee is more than just caffeine?

We often think of coffee as something quick and convenient, but little do we know the story behind it. Every cup is a journey filled with choices, people, and flavour. From the farm where coffee grows to the way it is processed, roasted, and brewed, every stage shapes what we eventually taste.

This talk explores the life of a coffee bean,from the different paths it can take during processing, to how roasting transforms its flavours, and how brewing extracts those flavours into our cup.
But coffee is more than just a score or a label. Specialty coffee is also about traceability,knowing where your coffee comes from, who produced it, and appreciating the intentionality behind every step.

A lot goes into coffee before it ever reaches your cup. And once we understand that journey, a cup of coffee becomes more than just a drink. It becomes an opportunity to slow down, pay attention, and appreciate the story behind what we tas
title: Brewing with intentionality  | Arjun Sethi | TEDxVIT Pune

description:
Entering the professional world often comes with frameworks, strategies, and a picture-perfect plan, but things can look very different when theory meets reality. Navigating a traditional industry means learning to adapt, question assumptions, and understand the people and systems already in place.

This talk explores the experience of stepping into the next generation, from identifying opportunities in overlooked markets to navigating change, learning from decades of experience, and understanding when established ways of working need to evolve.

But growth isn't always about building something new. Sometimes, the biggest opportunities lie within what already exists, if you are willing to look closely enough to find them.

A lot goes into navigating an established industry beyond what any textbook can teach. And once the frameworks meet reality, success becomes less about having all the right answers and more about knowing when to adapt, when to listen, and when to let the framework g
title: What it takes to reinvent a traditional business | Ishita Malpani | TEDxVIT Pune

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the problem is not how determined you are to reach your goal but the method you are using to get there?

For a time the way we learn engineering has been about following rules, solving problems that have already been defined and getting ready for a future that we think we can predict. The world outside of school is changing really fast. It is changing faster than the systems we learn in school can keep up with. Now if you want to build something with technology, start a company, get a job or just make something meaningful, there is one thing that's really important: being able to learn quickly.

In this talk Anuj Tiwari talks about Progressive-Aggressive Learning, a way of learning that combines two ideas that seem like they do not go together. It's about learning beyond memorization and about understanding why things are the way they are. It is about making yourself learn by using problems, setting deadlines for yourself, taking action and trying again and again.

Putting the
title: Why engineers learn too slowly for a fast-changing world. | Anuj Tiwari | TEDxRVCE

author: TEDx Talks
description: ¿Cuántas veces has tenido algo importante que decir y no lo dijiste? Sabías la respuesta en clase, querías defender algo injusto, querías empezar ese proyecto, y te quedaste en silencio. A los diez años, Daniela Ulloa tenía su propio negocio en una feria escolar: los productos estaban sobre la mesa y la dueña era ella, pero quien hablaba con los clientes era su mamá. Durante años creyó que ese miedo decía algo sobre quién era, que la valentía era un talento que otros tenían y ella no, y le tomó mucho tiempo entender que el problema nunca fue el miedo sino todo lo que ella creía que el miedo significaba. En esta charla propone una idea sencilla y difícil de aplicar: no actuamos porque nos sentimos valientes, empezamos a sentirnos valientes porque actuamos. Y comparte la regla que ordenó su forma de decidir, bautizada por la cantidad exacta con la que empezó de nuevo tras un momento muy duro: no arriesgarlo todo, sino identificar el riesgo más pequeño que uno pueda soportar y dar ese pa
title: La regla de los 68 dólares: de un riesgo pequeño a una vida distinta | Daniela Ulloa | TEDxUTMACH
